translation.title: Commentary on Sūrat "al-Kāfirūn." In the name of God, the Merciful, the Compassionate.

x: Discussion of the interpretation of the saying of God, glorified be His praise and hallowed be His names:

Say: O disbelievers (1) I do not worship what you worship (2) nor are you worshippers of what I worship (3) nor am I a worshipper of what you have worshipped (4) nor are you worshippers of what I worship (5) To you your religion, and for me my religion (6)

He, exalted be His mention, says to His prophet Muḥammad ﷺ. It was reported that the polytheists of his people proposed to him that they would worship God for a year, on condition that the Prophet of God ﷺ worship their gods for a year. So God sent down, informing him of the answer to them in this matter: Say, Muḥammad, to those polytheists who asked you to worship their gods for a year on condition that they worship your God for a year:
I do not worship what you worship
nor are you worshippers of what I worship
, in what I shall face in the future,
, in what you will face, for ever,
, I, now and in the future.

This was said in this way because the address from God to His Messenger ﷺ concerned particular individuals among the polytheists, of whom it was known that they would never believe, and this had been settled for them in His prior knowledge. So He commanded His prophet ﷺ [the printed text here reads "فأمَر نبيَّه صلى الله عليه وسلم اللَّهِ أن," in which "اللَّهِ" appears to be an intrusion] to make them despair of what they coveted and told themselves, and to tell them that this would not come about from him or from them at any time. He also made the Prophet of God ﷺ despair of coveting their belief and of their ever prospering. So they were, and they neither prospered nor succeeded, until some of them were killed by the sword on the day of Badr and some perished before that as disbelievers.
The people of interpretation said the same as we have said, and the reports have come to this effect.
Mention of those who said this:

c: Muḥammad b. Mūsā al-Ḥarashī told me, he said: Abū Khalaf told us, he said: Dāwūd told us, from ʿIkrima, from Ibn ʿAbbās.
m: Quraysh promised the Messenger of God ﷺ that they would give him wealth so that he would become the richest man in Mecca, and would marry him to whichever women he wished, and would tread on his heel [i.e., follow his lead]. They said to him: "This is yours with us, Muḥammad, but stop reviling our gods and do not mention them with evil. If you do not, we offer you one proposal, which holds some good for you and for us." He said: "What is it?" They said: "You worship our gods, al-Lāt and al-ʿUzzā, for a year, and we worship your God for a year." He said: "Wait until I see what comes from my Lord." Then the revelation came from the Preserved Tablet:
, the sūra. And God sent down:
Say: Is it other than God that you command me to worship, O ignorant ones?
Rather, worship God and be among the thankful

c: Yaʿqūb told me, he said: Ibn ʿUlayya told us, from Muḥammad b. Isḥāq, he said: Saʿīd b. Mīnā, the client of al-Bakhtarī [Fn 2], told me.
m: He said: al-Walīd b. al-Mughīra, al-ʿĀṣ b. Wāʾil, al-Aswad b. al-Muṭṭalib and Umayya b. Khalaf met the Messenger of God ﷺ and said: "Muḥammad, come, let us worship what you worship, and you worship what we worship, and we will make you a partner in our whole affair. If what you have brought is better than what we have, we will have shared it with you and taken our portion of it. If what we have is better than what is in your hands, you will have shared our affair with us and taken your portion of it." So God sent down

x: To you your religion, and for me my religion

. He, exalted be His mention, says: to you your religion, which you will never abandon, because it has been sealed upon you and He decreed that you would not part from it and that you would die upon it. And for me is my religion, which I follow and will never abandon, because it has passed in God's prior knowledge that I will not move from it to another.

c: Yūnus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said.
m: To you your religion, and for me my religion

, he said: it was addressed to the polytheists. He said: The Jews worship only God and do not associate partners with Him, except that they disbelieve in some of the prophets and in what they brought from God. They disbelieve in the Messenger of God and in what he brought from God, and they killed groups of the prophets unjustly and in enmity. He said: except for the remnant who survived until Nebuchadnezzar came out. They said: "ʿUzayr is the son of God, God's adopted one" (
) [Fn 2]. But they did not worship him [Fn 3], and did not do as the Christians did, who said: "The Messiah is the son of God" and worshipped him.

x: Some of the people of Arabic [Fn 4] used to say: He repeated His saying
I do not worship what you worship
and what follows it for emphasis, as in
Indeed with hardship comes ease (5) indeed with hardship comes ease
You will surely see the Hellfire (6) then you will surely see it with the eye of certainty

notes.en: The author transmitted it in his History (2/337). Al-Tabarani transmitted it in al-Saghir (1/265) through Abu Khalaf with this chain. Al-Suyuti attributed it in al-Durr al-Manthur (6/404) to Ibn Abi Hatim.
notes.ar: أخرجه المصنف في تاريخه 2/ 337، وأخرجه الطبراني في الصغير 1/ 265 من طريق أبي خلف به، وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 6/ 404 إلى ابن أبي حاتم.

notes.en: The author’s History reads “the client of Abu al-Bakhtari.” He is al-Bakhtari ibn Abi Dhibab, as stated in the biographical entry for Saʿid ibn Mina. See Tahdhib al-Kamal (11/84).
notes.ar: في تاريخ المصنف: "مولى أبى البختري". وهو البختري بنُ أبى ذباب كما في ترجمة سعيد بن مينا. ينظر تهذيب الكمال 11/ 84.

notes.en: The author transmitted it in his History (2/337). Al-Suyuti attributed it in al-Durr al-Manthur (6/404) to Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn al-Anbari in al-Masahif. See Sirat Ibn Hisham (1/362).
notes.ar: أخرجه المصنف في تاريخه 2/ 337، وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 6/ 404 إلى ابن أبي حاتم وابن الأنباري في المصاحف، وينظر سيرة ابن هشام 1/ 362.

notes.en: The manuscripts read “daʿa.” The adopted reading is correct, God willing.
notes.ar: في النسخ: "دعا". والمثبت هو الصواب إن شاء الله.

notes.en: Manuscripts S, T1, T2, and T3 read “yaʿbudu.”
This is al-Farraʾ, in Maʿani al-Qurʾan (3/288).
